pr_title: Update FillModel.MarketFill to prevent fills at stale prices
pr_body:
#### Description
- The default fill model for market orders has been updated to never return fills on stale data (e.g. fill-forward bars). Orders submitted after the latest data point will be filled at the open price of the next bar.
- The new MarketFillOnNextBarRegressionAlgorithm regression algorithm has been added.
- Some regression algorithms with frequent trading have been slightly changed to check for pending market orders and expected statistics have been updated.
- The default MarketFillTimeout has also been lowered from 5 seconds to 0.5 seconds (only for backtesting).

#### Related Issue
Closes #2762 

#### Motivation and Context
Market orders can be filled at stale prices in the following cases:
- using multiple assets at different resolutions and submitting a market order for the lower resolution symbol
- submitting market orders from scheduled events at times not aligned with the asset resolution

#### Requires Documentation Change
No.

#### How Has This Been Tested?
New regression test + existing unit and regression tests.

#### Types of changes
- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)
- [ ] Non-functional change (xml comments/documentation/etc)

issue_context.title: Market orders can be filled at stale prices in backtesting

review_comments:
It might be worth a little more thought into what happens with longer bars in live trading; e.g. minute or hourly. If it waits for the next bar to arrive the fill event _wall-clock-time_ could be delayed a full hour in paper trading, even though the event was at the start of the hour? Ideally; we should fill on the ticks in live-paper trading. 

Unfortunately, in backtesting this will have an impact too -- say you do "an event" on a fill - the backtest time of the fill and thus event trigger will be 1-Resolution step past the time of the market order.

Not sure of the solution to this but a market order should fill "instantly" (perhaps at _next bar open_ after the end of the AlgorithmManager Loop - looking ahead 1 step.. )

E.g. Perhaps we could pulse the bar-open price as a tick at the start of each bar... at the _start time_ of the bar.

Very interesting insights. Regarding live mode -- completely agreed should fill using the tick stream, the data for which should already be in the `SecurityCache`. Also, since live-mode pulses the algo loop _at least_ once a second, we're guaranteed to have the fill methods invoked within a second independent of the configured resolution.

One concern I have w/ pulsing open prices at the start of every bar is it might have the effect of cutting performance almost in half in backtest since we'll be spinning the algo manager loop 2x (once for open tick and once for bar). Backtesting sounds like the tougher case here, for live, was thinking could add an event that is raised each time the security's real-time price is updated and then fill models could add an event handler, wait for the next tick, create the fill, and then remove their event handler. I suppose we could _mock_ real-time price in backtest by doing something like linear regression between open/close of the bars? This would keep the 'look-ahead' logic in the data feed and prevent it from needing to creep into algo manager and other parts of the system. Certainly not  a solid idea, but just trying to add some off-the-wall ideas into the mix :)

Also, getting algo manager to look ahead might be tough, although I suppose he could always have the _next_ time step in hand and the 'current' loop would always be processing the _previous_ time step, so he'd be holding on to 2 time steps each loop (current/next).

Happy to bounce ideas around if you guys would like to chat :)

Wondering if requiring this line in our regression algorithms will break user algorithms without this line? In fact, I'm surprised this is required since we should be able to create the market fill _before_ we invoke `OnData` on the next time loop, BICBW
Seeing the total trades here change is unexpected.

Ideally, this should be 0 for backtesting as there are conditions/data where this delay could slow down backtests 100x; if 0 is there a chance in a low power/single threaded environment this could give indeterministic backtesting?
